At :172/:287 a late GET can undo an applied delta and lower sidebarRevision. app.svelte.js:518/:384 still saves only the last runtime delta during a registry read, losing earlier changed threads. runtime.go:245/:368 does not serialize snapshot capture through notify; concurrent publishers can publish new then old and partial deltas never correct it on unrelated changes.
P2: explorer.svelte.js:836/:885 leaves unchanged rows marked offline after an equal-revision reconnect. runtime.go:212 omits empty rows, producing {}, which asks browser consumers for whole-list reads again. Retained base issue in the changed hub: runtime.go:550 lets a later star's sidebarCurrent=true mask an earlier structural refresh.

REVIEW: FAIL on 75b8831a (tree hhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh). New commentary: uuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu.

The original four browser probes now pass. Runtime accumulation, the publication lock (including stars), empty-array wire format, and preserving the earlier rebuild need check out. No extra concurrency test is requested.

Two remaining P1 variants of the revision/epoch finding reproduce:
1. explorer.svelte.js:247 bootstrap calls commitActiveSidebar without the epoch gate. A bootstrap response at revision 50 held behind initialSessionsPromise can land after reconnect has installed revision 1 from a restarted server. It overwrites that new population and sets revision 50, making subsequent valid lower-revision reads fail the guard.
2. explorer.svelte.js:296 treats a read begun during the outage as current, because its epoch matches while link.up is false. Such a read reinstates the old revision after onStreamError cleared it. On reopen the new-process lower-revision repair is rejected. A same-server equal marker also leaves outage-read rows offline. Only a read belonging to the current live subscription can start its sequence; keep last-seen row filling separate.

P2: explorer.svelte.js:300/:1091 forgets a failed gap repair. If its GET fails once, then the stream stays healthy/quiet and catalogVersion is unchanged (runtime-only sidebar change), refocus does not retry. The old list remains indefinitely.

Three new disposable probes fail, in xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx, named bootstrap from old subscription, whole read during outage, and failed gap repair. They can run with the existing reviewer-slice1xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx Requested focused browser files plus sidebar_ordering passed (67 tests); focused Go and diff check passed. Code tree unchanged. Both revised deploy declarations are confirmed. Centralize epoch acceptance rather than requiring both callers to remember it. Full details are in the commentary. Please fix and prompt me for re-check.

REVIEW: FAIL on 62b50e92 (tree hhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh). Commentary: uuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu.

All seven earlier browser probes now pass. Central acceptance and the failure-only retry address round 2. Earlier runtime findings remain resolved. Focused browser tests plus sidebar_ordering passed (70 tests); focused Go and diff check passed. Both deploy declarations remain confirmed.

One P1 revision-continuity case remains on the real App startup path: explorer.svelte.js:188 considers the bootstrap read live because link starts up=true, although App.svelte:128 only creates the first catalog stream after bootstrap settles. A restart between the bootstrap GET's snapshot and the first stream connection causes no stream error. With old-process revision 1, a new-process revision-1 marker is trusted and leaves the wrong population. With old revision 50 and new revision 1, the marker asks for a GET, but the new lower-revision response is rejected. Because that GET succeeds, retry never runs. Initial bootstrap can be held behind initialSessionsPromise, so this gap includes the full wait, not just the finally callback.

Both cases reproduce in the new disposable table test in reviewer-slice1xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx: first stream connection after bootstrap from old process revision %i establishes a new baseline. Current probe results: 7 pass, 2 fail. Full path: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx No code edits.

The first baseline must belong to the actual stream subscription too; a read before the first connection cannot prove the server generation. Keep the shared acceptance rule. This is the remaining case of the original revision-continuity finding. Please fix and prompt me for re-check.

For xx-9999's 'read xxxxxxxxxxxxx once per page load': after your slice 1, a page still reads the list 3-4 times at boot (startPolling, the URL resolve, and the catalog stream's first open). I will cut that to 2 by letting the URL resolve and stream open join reads in flight; the stream-open read stays because the catalog stream sends no runtime state on connect. Exactly one would need the stream to send a runtime snapshot on connect (with absent = released semantics), which is your runtime-event format, so I will not touch it. If you want it in a later slice, say so; otherwise no reply needed. I will build on main after your slice 1 lands.
